sentences.text: His last drawn wages were Rs.28,999/-.
The Taj Group of Hotels is a part of the Indian Hotels Co. Ltd (IHCL) under the management of TATA.
The chain of Taj Group of Hotels spreads far and wide both within and outside India.
The balance sheet of the hotels are prepared commonly by the IHCL.
Therefore, all the units of IHCL should be treated and governed uniformly.
Hence, so far as the employees of the IHCL are concerned, they should be treated at par in all respect.
The retirement age of the ordinary employee on pay roll of the Indian Hotel Company in Delhi and Taj Bengal was 55 years whereas in Mumbai, it is 60 years.

sentences.text: Since the retirement age of employees in other companies under the brand name TATA is 60 years, there is no reason the same should not be adopted for the employee of IHCL uniformly.
The retired employees of the respondents amalgamated and formed The Taj Hotel Employees Association registered with registration No.1510/2016.
A legal notice dated 16.12.2013 was sent to the managements followed by legal notice of demand dated 10.02.2014 but no response was ever received.
All the demands of the workman was ignored by the management despite numerous reminders.
Conciliation proceedings initiated by the workman failed.

During the course of the conciliation proceedings, the management enhanced the retirement age to 58 years effective from 20th January, 2015 and further to 60 years thus, excluding the workman from the benefits of the enhancement of age of retirement, which is not only illegal and arbitrary but also amounts to unfair labour practice and shows the flippant attitude of the managements towards their retired employees who devoted major part of their life working for the managements.
All the employees who have ID NO. 422/2019 Anil Kumar Banaik vs. Taj Mahal Hotel & Ors. retired should be adequately compensated for the loss of years of service.

6. The written statements filed by management no.1 and management no. 2 are more or less the same.
As preliminary objections, it is submitted that the purported dispute as referred has not been properly espoused.

The Taj Hotel Employees Associations is not a legal entity and has no locus standi to raise any dispute, much less any industrial dispute, or file any claim, against the management on behalf of the workmen employed by the Taj Mahal Hotel or Indian Hotels Company Ltd.
The workmen employed with Taj Mahal Hotel or Indian Hotels Company Ltd are not members of the Association.
The Claimant falls out of the ambit of definition of "Workman" in Section 2 (s) of the Industrial Disputes Act (hereinafter 'the Act').
Before his retirement, the Claimant Sh. Anil Banaik was working as Assistant Restaurant Manager with Taj Palace Hotel and his last drawn salary exceeded Rs. 10,000/- per month.
